newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unions pledge struggle against Bonn cuts.
newsitem.headline: German unions pledge struggle against Bonn cuts.

text.p: The German Trade Union Federation (DGB) on Friday promised a long struggle against the government's austerity drive.

Speaking on German television ahead of nationwide weekend protests which are expected to attract 100,000 people, the DGB's deputy chairwoman Ursula Engelen-Kefer said unions needed "to take a deep breath".
She said the protests could have a decisive impact on a parliamentary vote on key parts of Bonn's spending cuts plans next Friday.

In particular, she said, plans to cut support for Job Creation Measures (ABMs) in east Germany could persuade some east German Christian Democrats members of parliament not to vote with the government.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's plans to override upper house objections to his austerity package by obtaining a "Chancellor Majority" -- or absolute majority of 337 votes -- in the lower house, or Bundestag next Friday.
Heiner Geissler, deputy chairman of the Christian Democrats parliamentary group, told German radio, however, that the government would have no problem getting the required majority.

The government's austerity package aims to slash public spending by 70 billion marks next year in a bid to get the public budget deficit low enough to qualify for the single European currency. The package also contains a host of supply-side measures aimed at lowering industry's costs.

"My sympathy lies not with those who may have to forego a rise in their incomes but rather with the four million unemployed," Geissler said, adding that the austerity package aimed to boost employment.
CDU general secretary Peter Hintze told reporters in Bonn that the country's social security system could only remain intact if all areas were open to review and necessary change.
The DGB expects 60,000 people to attend the main demonstration at Berlin's Brandeburg gate. Other protests will take place in Leipzig, Hamburg, Stuttgart, Ludwigshafen and Dortmung.
